name: VDSO Hijacking
description:
Adversaries may inject malicious code into processes via VDSO hijacking in order to evade process-based defenses as well as possibly elevate privileges. Virtual dynamic shared object (vdso) hijacking is a method of executing arbitrary code in the address space of a separate live process. 

VDSO hijacking involves redirecting calls to dynamically linked shared libraries. Memory protections may prevent writing executable code to a process via [Ptrace System Calls](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1055/008). However, an adversary may hijack the syscall interface code stubs mapped into a process from the vdso shared object to execute syscalls to open and map a malicious shared object. This code can then be invoked by redirecting the execution flow of the process via patched memory address references stored in a process' global offset table (which store absolute addresses of mapped library functions).(Citation: ELF Injection May 2009)(Citation: Backtrace VDSO)(Citation: VDSO Aug 2005)(Citation: Syscall 2014)

Running code in the context of another process may allow access to the process's memory, system/network resources, and possibly elevated privileges. Execution via VDSO hijacking may also evade detection from security products since the execution is masked under a legitimate process.

telemetry.name: Module Load
telemetry.description: A module or library being loaded into a running process.
telemetry.collection_focus: Scope Sysmon ImageLoad (7) to lab processes/paths; retain module hash, signer and destination process. Inventory alone does not prove a module loaded.

providers.scope: Linux alternative for supported system-call and file events; different semantics and fields.

configuration: On a disposable Windows host, review the installed Sysmon schema and current configuration; merge scoped event filters into the existing policy rather than replacing it.
Forward Microsoft-Windows-Sysmon/Operational to the lab collector. Preserve event ID, timestamp, computer, process identifiers and the original event.
For Linux or macOS, select the equivalent sensor separately and test its emitted fields; a Windows event ID does not transfer across platforms.

telemetry.description: Instrumented operating-system API calls and their return values.
telemetry.collection_focus: Use an approved EDR trace or instrument the owned lab process at selected APIs. Define API name, caller, sanitized arguments and return status.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

telemetry.collection_focus: Collect Sysmon ProcessCreate (1); preserve ProcessGuid and parent identifiers. Security 4688 is an alternative with separate audit/command-line settings.

strategies.name: Detection Strategy for VDSO Hijacking on Linux

analytics.name: Analytic 1241
analytics.guidance: Detects the redirection of syscall execution flow via modification of VDSO code stubs or GOT entries to load and execute a malicious shared object through mmap and ptrace.

tuning.description: Regex to filter dynamic library paths outside of `/lib`, `/usr/lib`, etc. (e.g., `/tmp`, `/dev/shm`)
Max delay allowed between ptrace attach and mmap/mprotect execution in target process
Flag when executable memory mappings deviate from normal runtime behavior
Parent processes unlikely to legitimately call ptrace (e.g., nginx, apache2, sshd)

mitigations.description: Some endpoint security solutions can be configured to block some types of process injection based on common sequences of behavior that occur during the injection process.
